from.place: Paragraph 2, displayed derived coefficient-adjunction and inverse-limit calculation, and the following naturality and triangle-identity sentences; foundational enhancement of finite coefficient adjunction diagrams. Technical input: Pinched simplices give a weakly equivalent mapping resolution. Smaller input: Derived ordinary adjunction and counit criterion for Quillen equivalences. Independent ordinary homotopy-category proof, without the descendant infinity-adjunction theorem.

title: Derived ordinary adjunction and counit criterion for Quillen equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ be model categories with functorial factorizations, using the model-category and cofibrant/fibrant conventions of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be an ordinary adjunction such that $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. Write $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)=\mathcal M[W_{\mathcal M}^{-1}]$ and similarly for $\mathcal N$, where the localization functor sends every member of $W$ to an isomorphism and, by precomposition, identifies functors out of the localization with functors that invert $W$, including their natural transformations. Cofibrant and fibrant replacements define functors $\mathbf LL:\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)\to\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal N)$ and $\mathbf RU$ in the reverse direction, and an adjunction $\mathbf LL\dashv\mathbf RU$. If $\mathbf LL$ is an equivalence of categories, then for every fibrant $Y\in\mathcal N$ and every cofibrant replacement $q:QUY\to UY$ (a weak equivalence with cofibrant source), the composite $LQUY\xrightarrow{Lq}LUY\xrightarrow{\epsilon_Y}Y$ is a weak equivalence. In particular if $UY$ is cofibrant then the ordinary adjunction counit $\epsilon_Y:LUY\to Y$ itself is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Lemma 1.3.10, Proposition 1.3.13(b)-(c) and proof of Corollary 1.3.14, printed pp. 18-20. No Stacks tag states the model-category criterion.

proof.text: We use the model axioms in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Lifting classes are closed under composition and pushout/pullback in the appropriate direction: solve the constituent lifting squares and use the universal property. They contain isomorphisms, so $W$ contains identities. Since $L\dashv U$, a lifting square against $U(p)$ transposes to a lifting square against $p$ with left map $L(i)$. The preservation hypotheses on $L$ therefore imply that $U$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Left adjoints preserve initial objects and coproducts, and right adjoints preserve terminal objects and products, directly from the adjunction Hom bijection. Consequently $L$ preserves cofibrant objects and $U$ preserves fibrant objects.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; elementary lifting-adjunction argument (Hovey Lemma 1.3.4).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to a weak equivalence $f:A\to B$ between cofibrant objects. Write $f=pi$ with $p$ a trivial fibration and $s:B\to Z$ a cofibration section. Two-out-of-three gives $i,s\in C\cap W$. Thus $L(i),L(s)\in W$; $L(p)L(s)=1$ gives $L(p)\in W$, and $L(f)=L(p)L(i)\in W$. For a weak equivalence $g:A\to B$ between fibrant objects, the dual split factorization $g=pi$, $ri=1$, has $p,r\in F\cap W$. Hence $U(p),U(r)\in W$, $U(r)U(i)=1$ gives $U(i)\in W$, and $U(g)\in W$. The required retract and two-out-of-three axioms are exactly those in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; Brown preservation argument, Hovey Lemma 1.1.12 (split factorizations verified in Mathlib BrownLemma.lean:48-87,97-134).

proof.text: Choose functorial cofibrant replacements $q_X:QX\to X$ as trivial fibrations and fibrant replacements $r_Y:Y\to RY$ as trivial cofibrations, using [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Naturality of these weak equivalences and two-out-of-three show that $Q$ and $R$ preserve $W$. Step 2 then makes $\gamma_{\mathcal N}LQ$ and $\gamma_{\mathcal M}UR$ invert $W$. The localization universal property in the item defines functors $\mathbf LL$ and $\mathbf RU$ from these two functors. If $A$ is cofibrant, $L(q_A)$ is a weak equivalence by Step 2, giving $\mathbf LL(\gamma A)\cong\gamma(LA)$. If $B$ is fibrant, $U(r_B)$ is a weak equivalence, giving $\mathbf RU(\gamma B)\cong\gamma(UB)$. These comparisons are natural because $q$ and $r$ are natural.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; replacement/localization construction, Hovey Definition 1.3.6 and Lemma 1.3.10.

proof.text: For cofibrant $A$ and fibrant $B$, the ordinary adjunction bijection between maps $LA\to B$ and $A\to UB$ respects and reflects equality after localization, as follows. By [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test], an equality between maps $LA\to B$ is represented on a good path object of $B$. Its image under $U$ is a good path object of $UB$: $U$ preserves products and fibrations, and preserves its section weak equivalence by Step 2 since the path object is fibrant (it fibrates over the fibrant product $B\times B$). Transposing the path homotopy gives a path homotopy between the adjoint maps. Conversely an equality between the adjoint maps is represented on a good cylinder of $A$. Its image under $L$ is a good cylinder of $LA$: $L$ preserves coproducts and cofibrations, and preserves its contraction weak equivalence by Step 2 since its total object is cofibrant. Transposing gives a cylinder homotopy between the original maps. Good cylinders and paths exist by factoring the fold $A\amalg A\to A$ and diagonal $B\to B\times B$ using [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. The same cited homotopy test makes both transposed homotopies equalities in the required localizations.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; explicit descent of the adjunction Hom bijection using good homotopies; Hovey Proposition 1.2.5 and proof of Lemma 1.3.10.

proof.text: [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective] (applied in both model categories, with $LA$ cofibrant and $UB$ fibrant by Step 1) and Step 4 give a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal N)}(\gamma LA,\gamma B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)}(\gamma A,\gamma UB)$ for cofibrant $A$ and fibrant $B$. Apply it to $A=QX$, $B=RY$, and compose with the isomorphisms $\gamma(q_X)$ and $\gamma(r_Y)$. This gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf LL(\gamma X),\gamma Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\gamma X,\mathbf RU(\gamma Y))$. Its formula on a representative is ordinary adjunction followed by these replacement isomorphisms, so naturality follows from ordinary adjunction and naturality of $q,r$. Naturality extends to the localization: the naturality equation for the inverse of an inverted map follows by multiplying its naturality equation by the inverse on both sides. Equivalently, use the universal property for natural transformations stipulated in the item, one variable at a time. A natural Hom bijection is precisely an ordinary adjunction; thus these bijections give $\mathbf LL\dashv\mathbf RU$.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; construction of the ordinary derived adjunction, Hovey Lemma 1.3.10, without any infinity-category truncation.

proof.text: Let $Y$ be fibrant, so $UY$ is fibrant by Step 1. For the chosen trivial-fibration replacement $q_0:Q(UY)\to UY$, the ordinary adjunction sends $e_0=\epsilon_Y\circ L(q_0):LQ(UY)\to Y$ to $q_0:Q(UY)\to UY$: indeed $U(\epsilon_Y)\circ UL(q_0)\circ\eta_{Q(UY)}=U(\epsilon_Y)\circ\eta_{UY}\circ q_0=q_0$. Here the first equality is naturality of $\eta$, and the second is an ordinary triangle identity. Under the Hom bijection of Step 5 and the fibrant/cofibrant comparisons of Step 3, $\gamma(q_0)$ becomes the identity of the object represented by $UY$. Hence $\gamma(e_0)$ is the counit component of the derived adjunction, after the indicated representation isomorphisms. This identifies the actual map, rather than only its source and target.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; explicit counit transpose calculation, Hovey Lemma 1.3.10 and Proposition 1.3.13(b)-(c).

proof.text: If $\mathbf LL$ is an equivalence, [lem-coef-adjunction-equivalence-counit-iso] says that the counit of the adjunction in Step 5 is a natural isomorphism. Step 6 therefore shows that $\gamma_{\mathcal N}(e_0)$ is an isomorphism. We next prove directly from ordinary homotopies that a map with invertible localization image is a weak equivalence; this avoids the existing detection node, whose dependencies lead back to the present item.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; categorical counit fact, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/FullyFaithful.lean:247-249; Hovey Proposition 1.3.13.

proof.text: Let $v:X\to Y$ be any map in either model category with $\gamma(v)$ invertible. Use the functorial replacements of Step 3 to put $A=RQX$, $B=RQY$, $f=RQ(v)$. Both $A,B$ are cofibrant and fibrant, since $QX\to RQX$ and $QY\to RQY$ are trivial cofibrations. The naturality identities $q_YQ(v)=vq_X$ and $f r_{QX}=r_{QY}Q(v)$ imply that $\gamma(f)$ is invertible. Factor $f=pi$ with $i:A\to E$ a trivial cofibration and $p:E\to B$ a fibration. Then $E$ is also cofibrant and fibrant, and $\gamma(p)$ is invertible. These factorizations and object properties use only [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; independent ordinary saturation proof, Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv), replacement and fibration-factor reduction.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective], since $B$ is cofibrant and $E$ fibrant, represent $\gamma(p)^{-1}$ by a map $s:B\to E$. By [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test], the equality $\gamma(ps)=1$ gives a homotopy $H:I\to B$ on a chosen good cylinder $B\xrightarrow{a_0,a_1}I\xrightarrow{c}B$ with $Ha_0=ps$, $Ha_1=1_B$. As $B$ is cofibrant, $a_0$ is a cofibration; $ca_0=1_B$ and $c\in W$ make it a trivial cofibration. The square with top $s$, left $a_0$, right $p$, and bottom $H$ has a lift $V:I\to E$ by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Thus $t=Va_1$ satisfies $pt=1_B$, and necessarily $\gamma(t)=\gamma(p)^{-1}$. The lifting square is valid because $p$ is the fibration factor from Step 8.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; ordinary saturation: homotopy inverse rectified to a strict section by a specified lifting square (Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv)).

proof.text: Now $\gamma(tp)=1_{\gamma E}$. Applying [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] to the cofibrant and fibrant object $E$ gives a cylinder $E\xrightarrow{b_0,b_1}J\xrightarrow{d}E$ and $G:J\to E$ with $Gb_0=tp$, $Gb_1=1_E$, $db_0=db_1=1_E$, and $d\in W$. Two-out-of-three makes $b_0,b_1,G$ weak equivalences, and then $tp=Gb_0\in W$. In the arrow category $p:E\to B$ is a retract of $tp:E\to E$: the maps have components $(1_E,t)$ and $(1_E,p)$, and their composite on $p$ is $(1_E,pt)=(1_E,1_B)$. Retract closure gives $p\in W$ and then $f=pi\in W$. Finally $f r_{QX}=r_{QY}Q(v)$ gives $Q(v)\in W$, and $vq_X=q_YQ(v)$ gives $v\in W$. All weak-equivalence deductions use the two-out-of-three and retract axioms in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure].

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; ordinary saturation: homotopy-to-identity, explicit arrow retract, and both replacement squares (Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv)).

proof.text: Apply the detection argument of Steps 8-10 to $e_0$ from Step 7; it is a weak equivalence. Now let $q:C\to UY$ be the arbitrary cofibrant replacement allowed in the item; it need not be a fibration. Since $C$ is cofibrant and $q_0:Q(UY)\to UY$ is a trivial fibration, [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] supplies a lift $a:C\to Q(UY)$ with $q_0a=q$. Two-out-of-three gives $a\in W$; its two endpoints are cofibrant, so Step 2 gives $L(a)\in W$. Consequently $\epsilon_Y L(q)=e_0 L(a)$ is a weak equivalence. This proves the claim for every weak-equivalence replacement with cofibrant source, as stated.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; Hovey Proposition 1.3.13(b)-(c), with the comparison lift needed for arbitrary replacements explicitly supplied.

proof.text: If $UY$ is cofibrant, take the allowed replacement to be $q=1_{UY}$. Its counit composite is $\epsilon_Y:LUY\to Y$ itself, so Step 11 gives the final clause.

source.place: Paragraph 2 foundation; Hovey Corollary 1.3.14, identity-replacement specialization.
